title: How Business Central Integrates with Microsoft Excel (2025)

chapters.title: Opening and accessing data in Excel
Creating pivot tables and charts for analysis
Updating records in Excel and the addin pane
Publishing changes back to Business Central

features.name: Export data to Excel
features.description: Users can easily export data from Business Central list pages to Excel for analysis using Excel's data analysis tools.

features.name: Open or Edit in Excel option
features.description: On list pages, users have options to either open data in Excel for viewing or edit in Excel for making changes. Both Excel for the web and Excel app for Windows are supported.

features.name: Pivot table creation
features.description: Users can create pivot tables in Excel from Business Central data using Excel's insert tab with a simple drag and drop experience to analyze and visualize data like quarterly sales by customer.

features.name: Pivot chart visualization
features.description: Users can add pivot charts to their Excel reports to visualize Business Central data with a few clicks from the insert tab.

features.name: Data connection refresh
features.description: Reports and charts created in Excel are connected to Business Central data and can be refreshed to ensure they always reflect up-to-date information.

features.name: Bulk update in Excel
features.description: Users can update multiple records in Business Central by editing data in Excel and publishing the changes back, enabling efficient bulk updates that would be time-consuming if done individually.

features.name: Excel addin pane
features.description: When opening data in edit mode, the Excel addin pane displays controls to refresh, filter, and publish data between Excel and Business Central.
